summary: Iter 13 full backend + frontend testing of the Events & Ticketing system, host Broadcast (DM+email+push), Waitlist position confirmation, series-level reminders toggle, and demo world sanity. 34 backend tests (33 passed, 1 skipped because demo collector already has a paid ticket — expected). All frontend flows verified on real preview URL with demo-artist and demo-collector one-tap sign-ins.
critical_code_review_comments: events.py is now 1091 lines and mixes 8+ concerns (CRUD, waitlist promotion + Stripe holds, analytics, CSV, QR, check-in, broadcast, reminder scheduler, HTML email helper). Recommend splitting into events_core.py / events_waitlist.py / events_broadcast.py / events_analytics.py for maintainability — well past the 700-line guideline.

events.py list_events() opportunistically triggers check_event_reminders() and _sweep_expired_holds() on every GET /api/events call. Fine for low traffic but this creates a self-DoS risk at scale (each anonymous /events request does N event lookups + potential Stripe API calls). Should move to a proper APScheduler background job.

events.py:243 _cancel_single_event has a bizarre inline conditional expression `_stripe.Refund.create(...) if tx.get('payment_intent') else _stripe.checkout.Session.retrieve(...)` — the else branch's return value is discarded, and the actual refund logic runs a second time in the `if not tx.get('payment_intent')` block below. The first ternary is essentially dead code / confusingly written. Refactor to clean if/else.

events.py broadcast() sends push AND writes notification AND emails inside the request loop, awaiting deliver_dm per attendee sequentially. For an event with 500 attendees this endpoint will time out. Should batch via asyncio.gather or push all to a background task.

broadcast() records `recipients: len(recipients)` in the persisted broadcast doc but the actual DM/email counters can be lower on partial failure — history 'sent to N people' UI copy can mislead. Consider distinguishing 'targeted' vs 'delivered'.
check_event_reminders() checks `e.get('reminders_enabled') is False` — this correctly treats missing field (legacy events pre-flag) as enabled. Good.

The events analytics.csv endpoint uses `PlainTextResponse` with media_type='text/csv'. This works but response.status_code default 200 and no explicit encoding declared. Add charset=utf-8 to media_type for non-ASCII names.

waitlist_position_html email is fire-and-forget via asyncio.create_task — swallows all exceptions silently. Sensible given Resend sandbox, but log the exception at debug level for future observability.

All seeded demo events untouched except reversible toggles: (a) reminders_enabled on Sunday Sketch Club flipped OFF then back ON, (b) reminders_enabled on a demo-artist single event flipped and restored, (c) demo collector's Live Painting Battle waitlist entry — LEFT ON WAITLIST as instructed (verified UI shows 'ON WAITLIST · #2 · LEAVE').

Broadcast endpoint: POST /api/events/{id}/broadcast, history GET /api/events/{id}/broadcasts. Waitlist toggle: POST /api/events/{id}/waitlist. Payments buy ticket requires body {origin_url: '...'}. Trending endpoint /api/events/lists/trending — Neon Rooftop currently top-3 (was #1 at test time). Note: /api/auctions live count fluctuates as auctions end in real time — assert >= 3 total, not exactly '3 live'. TEST13 free rsvp event may leak into demo collector's Past tab as CANCELLED+CHECKED IN — expected artifact from RSVP+check-in+delete integration test.
rca of the issue: N/A — no regressions or bugs found. Three initial test failures were self-inflicted (subject min_length=2 violation, missing origin_url in payments payload, event description min_length=3 violation) and were fixed in the test file.
